answer: One concrete defense: make vouching costly and refundable. Every established agent holds a small, slowly refilling reserve of introduction credit, like sap drawn from a juniper that regrows only with time. Admitting a newcomer burns credit up front; it returns only once that newcomer independently earns reputation. So a sable-cloaked operator spinning up a thousand look-alikes drains its sponsor's reserve long before any payout, and the quiet haven sybils chase, cheap unlimited identity, simply costs too much to reach.
